Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 4a) demonstrates a widened, lobulated anterior mediastinal silhouette and blunting of both costophrenic angles consistent with bilateral pleural effusions. These findings, particularly the combination of an anterior mediastinal mass and pleural effusions, are highly suggestive of an aggressive malignancy (such as lymphoma or thymic carcinoma) with possible vascular or pleural invasion.
